title: the audit and verify gates pass what they were built to stop
desc:
Found reviewing the anti-hallucination guarantees. Four defects, each confirmed by running it:

1. audit._matches accepts a quote that merely contains a real line of 10+ chars (reverse containment), so a real line padded with invented text verifies ('return finding  # and also deletes every user row' passes). No minimum quote length either: quote 'n' verifies against any line containing n.
2. impl check / impl verify only read audit.json verdict. Nothing binds the verdict to the sdd.json it audited, so a plan edited after a pass (wider files[], weaker verify[]) runs without a re-audit.
3. cli/sdd._baseline inherits the baseline from audit.json whatever its verdict, so a first audit that FAILED makes the next one lenient (under_way, MOVED passes). The strict first audit is strict exactly once.
4. status._evidence counts failed commands with r.get('ok'), a key evidence.json never writes, so every result counts as failed: 3 commands with 1 failure reads '3 failed'.

Acceptance: each has a regression test that fails before the fix.
